\---  
title: Solving Multi-Product Vehicle Routing Problem with Changeover Costs using Mixed Integer Linear Programming  
contributors: Vinasétan Ratheil H., Rosas B.  
year: 2025  
paper link:   
github: [https://github.com/uac-rrteam/MPVRP-CC-modeling](https://github.com/uac-rrteam/MPVRP-CC-modeling)  
\---

\# Description

This work addresses the Multi-Product Vehicle Routing Problem with Changeover Costs (MPVRP-CC), a complex supply chain optimization problem arising in industries such as petroleum, chemical manufacturing, and food distribution, where vehicles must deliver multiple products from several depots to geographically dispersed customers while managing product changes between successive trips. We propose a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulation that jointly considers multi-depot distribution, heterogeneous fleets, split deliveries, depot inventory constraints, bounded multi-trip operations, and the cleaning and preparation costs associated with product changeovers. The model organizes vehicle operations into product-specific mini-routes connected through depot transfers and changeover decisions, while a bounded-trip structure helps control the search space and maintain feasibility. The formulation is evaluated with Gurobi on 150 synthetic benchmark instances designed to represent realistic supply chain configurations. In addition to the optimization model, an open experimental platform is developed to support benchmark generation, visualization, feasibility checking, and online evaluation, providing a reproducible foundation for comparing future exact, decomposition, and metaheuristic approaches to complex multi-product logistics problems.

\---  
title: Automatic epileptic seizures types detection from electroencephalograms  
contributors: Marie Mélène S. T., Vinasétan Ratheil H.  
year: 2025  
paper link:   
github:  
\---

\# Description

This work is focused on automatic epileptic seizures types detection from electroencephalograms. The main goal is to develop a tool for automatic epileptic seizures types detection. The expected contributions are introduction of local epileptic EEG corpus, and new approaches or models for automatic EEG analysis in epilepsy.    
This work is an intersection of neurology, neurosciences, computer science and AI.

My name is Merveilleux Gandaho Azihou and I am a Master's student in Software Engineering at the Institute for Training and Research in Computer Science (IFRI), University of Abomey-Calavi, Benin. I am currently a research intern at the Computer Science and Applications Research Laboratory (LRSIA), where I work on the design of modular software architectures for the orchestration of machine learning models applied to EEG signal analysis.

I completed my undergraduate studies in Computer Systems and Software Engineering at Le Faucon de Calavi Higher School, graduating with highest honors and the jury's congratulations. Previously, I worked as a Web Developer at Case\&Co., an IT Operations Agent at Ressources Plus, and completed several academic internships focused on software engineering and web development.

My primary research interests include software architecture, machine learning systems, scientific software engineering, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), and the development of extensible and reproducible software platforms for data analysis.

**Maryse Fortune Doloresse GAHOU** is a PhD student at the École Doctorale des Sciences de l'Ingénieur (ED-SDI), Université d'Abomey-Calavi (UAC), Bénin. Her doctoral research focuses on developing an interpretable machine learning system for early detection of chronic kidney disease (CKD) using clinical data from the Nephrology Department of CNHU-HKM, Benin's national referral hospital. Her work is supervised by Dr. Vinasetan Ratheil Esse Houndji (IFRI/UAC) and co-supervised by Prof. Jacques Vigan, Head of the Nephrology and Hemodialysis Department at CNHU-HKM.

Maryse also serves as Deputy Head of IT at FRIARE (Ratheil Foundation for Responsible and Efficient Artificial Intelligence in Africa), and teaches part-time at IFRI.

My name is Todè Rosas Behoundja, and I am a research intern with interests at the intersection of artificial intelligence, operations research, and combinatorial optimization. My work focuses on developing computational methods for solving complex decision and optimization problems, with particular interest in vehicle routing, mathematical programming, and metaheuristic approaches under the supervision of Dr. Ratheil Houndji.

I am in my final year of Bachelor’s degree in Artificial Intelligence at the Institut de Formation et de Recherche en Informatique (IFRI), University of Abomey-Calavi. Beyond operations research, I am interested in machine learning, intelligent systems, and speech and language processing.

I enjoy building reproducible computational tools that connect theoretical models with practical applications, and my broader research goal is to explore how artificial intelligence and optimization can support efficient decision-making for real-world problems.
